node.label: Rogers Brubaker
node.date_label: Citizenship and Nationhood in France and Germany (1992) · Nationalism Reframed (1996) · “Beyond ‘Identity’,” with Frederick Cooper (2000)
node.description: Investigates citizenship, nationhood and the analytical work performed by identity categories. With Frederick Cooper, he distinguishes people’s use of identity in political life from an analyst’s assumption that everyone possesses an identity or belongs to an already coherent group. Their alternative vocabulary separates identification, categorization, self-understanding and variable groupness. Their account of states emphasizes the power to impose administrative categories while refusing to equate that power with complete control of self-identification. Historical comparisons of France/Germany and postimperial Europe form part of this cross-disciplinary research.

proposed_edges.relationship: With Frederick Cooper, distinguishes identity as a political/practical category from the analytical processes of identification, categorization and variable groupness.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Primary article opening pp. 1–2 and selected “In other words” / “Identification and categorization” section pp. 14–17 read in an explicitly identified OCR mirror. This is conceptual differentiation, not a dismissal of identity politics or all historical experience.

proposed_edges.relationship: With Cooper, analyzes the state’s power to impose classifications while distinguishing external categorization from people’s self-identifications.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Joint primary pp. 15–17: state resources support official categories, but states do not monopolize identification and categories do not automatically produce homogeneous groups. Historical examples/referenced authors were not independently audited.
